label: Phase 1 gate - incentive spend linked to a VIN

label: Phase 1 gate - dealer code crosswalk coverage
caveat: Set level with the VIN link, because a claim can only be de-duplicated once both the car and the dealer resolve to one identity. The two together are what makes a duplicate provable.

label: Phase 1 gate - duplicate flags that are real
caveat: A false duplicate withholds an honest dealer's money, so precision is gated harder than recall. Measured on used-car adverts, an exact rule scored 98.7% precision and a relaxed one 20.7% (er_exact_precision, er_relax_precision), so 90% is where a scored match with a review band is working rather than either extreme. Those rates do not transfer to claims data.

label: Phase 1 gate - real duplicates that get flagged
caveat: Missing a duplicate costs money once; wrongly flagging one costs a dealer relationship, so recall is set below precision and the rest is caught in the human review band. The measured design clears it with room: automatic linking above the upper threshold caught 80.3% and the worked review band 96.0% (er_auto_link_recall, er_review_band_recall).

label: Phase 2 gate - ledger against the general ledger
caveat: Finance will not certify a benefit out of a ledger it cannot tie to the books. This is the gate that makes every later euro figure arguable in a committee rather than only in a model.

label: Phase 2 gate - retention uplift over a randomised control group
caveat: Deliberately set below the 3pp the value-at-risk model assumes (upgrade_capture_uplift, range 1-6pp), so the pilot can come in under the assumption and still pass, and so that failing the gate is a real possibility rather than a formality.

label: Phase 2 gate - confidence required on that uplift
caveat: A randomised control group is the only thing that turns the assumed euros of leak 2 into a measured number, so the standard is the conventional one and the holdout must be preserved.

label: Phase 3 gate - business cost of residual error against baseline
caveat: Measured against the Phase 2 baseline, not against a forecast. It is set on the cost of being wrong rather than on model error, because the evidence says level risk is about eight times curve risk and a better model cannot touch the level.

label: Phase 3 gate - adherence to the engine's recommendations
caveat: Below this the recommendations are not really being used, so any benefit measured is not the programme's. Paired with override payoff, which is tracked without a target in Year 1 because a well-judged override is a good outcome, not a failure.

label: Phase 4 exit - run-rate benefits certified by Finance
caveat: Set above the 27.7m euro a controls layer recovers from process leakage alone, so the gate cannot be passed on Phase 1's work; about four times the 20m euro ask.

label: KPI - days to settle an incentive claim
caveat: A controls layer that holds claims for review only works if the review is fast; a slow one gets overridden by the business and the control stops existing.

label: KPI - record pairs sent to human review
caveat: A capacity limit, not an accuracy one: it is what a review team can actually work. The measured threshold sweep put 8,344 pairs in the band on used-car adverts (er_review_band_pairs), which is what sizing this on real claims would look like.

label: KPI - market drift carried unseen between re-marks
caveat: Sits between the two measured cadences: 3.0% of level can drift unseen at today's quarterly review and 1.3% at monthly (level_3m_p5, level_1m_p5). Set between them so the target is reachable but not free, and so it is an exposure measure rather than a claimed saving.

label: KPI - error on thin slices against established markets
caveat: New brands, new markets and electrified lines are where borrowing data pays; the measured gain is 4.3% at 100 local cars and nothing by 250 (pooling_gain_100, pooling_gain_250), so the target is closing a gap, not reaching parity.

label: Design choice - band within which a pricer may adjust the recommendation
caveat: People use an imperfect algorithm far more when they can modify its output even slightly (Dietvorst, Simmons & Massey 2018), so the band exists to get the engine used at all. It is narrow because the evidence says the level, not the pricer, is what moves value.

label: Investment released at the start of Phase 1
caveat: Four tranches tied to the four phase gates, so the committee can stop after any one of them. The shape follows the work: build in Phases 1-2, scale in Phase 3, hand over in Phase 4.

label: Investment released at the Phase 1 gate
caveat: The largest tranche, because Phase 2 runs the ledger build and the randomised upgrade pilots at the same time.

label: Investment released at the Phase 2 gate
caveat: Scaling to the core markets, once the ledger reconciles and the uplift has been measured against a control group.

label: Investment released at the Phase 3 gate
caveat: The smallest tranche: Phase 4 is closing the loop and retiring a legacy system, not building.
